claims.statement: In the Atlas Administration API a database user's password is a write-only string of at least 8 characters, described as an alphanumeric string that authenticates the user against its database with SCRAM-SHA, and it does not appear in responses.

sources.supports: CloudDatabaseUser.password: 'Alphanumeric string that authenticates this database user against the database specified in databaseName ... This parameter doesn't appear in this response.' minLength 8, writeOnly

claims.statement: The password is a value the caller supplies when creating the database user (it is a request parameter), not a value Atlas generates in a documented format.

sources.supports: CloudDatabaseUser.password is a writeOnly request property: 'To authenticate with SCRAM-SHA, you must specify this parameter.'

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Included to give the database password its own claims, separate from API keys and service accounts. It adds no bare-value format.

openQuestions.question: Does Atlas accept only alphanumeric passwords, or does 'Alphanumeric string' loosely describe a wider set? The description does not say whether other characters are rejected, so the minimum length is the only structural fact; no grammar can be asserted.

A database password is user-chosen and has no documented prefix or shape, so it is not attributable to Atlas as a bare value; it is recognisable only in context such as a connection string. That context is covered by existing generic connection-string cases rather than by this family.
